questions.question: Is the main() method mandatory in every Java class?

Every object must have a main method

questions.correct_answer: B. No, only the class that needs to be executed directly requires it
questions.explanation: A Java class can exist without a main() method. However, if you want to run the class directly using the JVM (java ClassName), it must contain a valid main() method.

questions.question: Which is the correct signature of the main() method?
questions.correct_answer: C. public static void main(String[] args)
questions.explanation: The JVM looks for exactly public static void main(String[] args)

questions.question: Which of the following is a valid Java class name?

questions.question: What happens if a class does not contain a main() method and you try to run it?
questions.correct_answer: B. Runtime Error: Main method not found
questions.explanation: The class will compile successfully, but when executed, the JVM throws: Error: Main method not found in class ...

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of JIT (Just-In-Time) Compiler?

To convert bytecode into machine code during execution for better performance

questions.correct_answer: D. To convert bytecode into machine code during execution for better performance
questions.explanation: JIT is a part of the JVM. It converts frequently executed bytecode into native machine code, making Java programs run faster.  > ⚠️ This question appears twice (Q16 and Q17) in the test with identical content.

questions.question: Why should hardcoding values be avoided in Java applications?

It is required by the JVM

questions.correct_answer: C. It makes maintenance and configuration difficult
questions.explanation: Hardcoded values (database URLs, passwords, file paths, etc.) make applications difficult to maintain. Such values should be stored in configuration files, environment variables, or properties files.

questions.question: Why is Java called a Platform Independent language?

Java works only on Windows and Linux

questions.correct_answer: C. Java bytecode can run on any platform that has a JVM
questions.explanation: When Java code is compiled, it is converted into bytecode (.class file). This bytecode is not specific to any operating system. Any machine with a JVM (Java Virtual Machine) can execute it. This is the reason behind Java's famous principle: "Write Once, Run Anywhere (WORA)".

questions.question: Where are objects stored in Java memory?
questions.explanation: Objects created using the new keyword are stored in the Heap Memory. The reference variable may be stored elsewhere, but the actual object resides in the heap.

questions.question: Where are local variables stored?
questions.explanation: Local variables declared inside methods are stored in the Stack Memory and are automatically removed when the method execution completes.

questions.question: What is a common use case of a static variable in Java?
questions.correct_answer: B. Storing data shared by all objects of a class
questions.explanation: Static variables belong to the class, not to individual objects. Only one copy exists and is shared by all objects.

questions.question: What is the scope of a local variable in Java?
questions.correct_answer: C. Only within the method/block where it is declared
questions.explanation: A local variable can be accessed only inside the method, constructor, or block in which it is declared. It cannot be accessed outside that scope.

questions.explanation: A class without main() compiles successfully. The JVM requires main() only when you try to run that class directly.

A software company starts a new project. Before writing any code, the team meets with the client to understand business requirements, features, and user expectations.

questions.question: What is a JAR file in Java?
questions.correct_answer: B. Java Archive file used to package Java classes and resources
questions.explanation: A JAR (Java Archive) bundles compiled classes and resources into a single distributable file.

questions.question: Which command is used to create a JAR file?
questions.explanation: `jar cvf app.jar *.class`: c = create, v = verbose, f = output file name.
